reviewer: Codex UI sub-agent; AI visual review, not a human or team sign-off
scope: Historical visual-only review of the original attempt1 PNGs; superseded for final acceptance by the requested fresh attempt2.
review_method: Opened all 26 original PNGs individually with view_image, in pairs of the two viewports. Computed raw SHA256 and actual PNG IHDR dimensions and compared all with browser/result.json. No screenshot was edited, resized or regenerated for this review.
shared_observations: Both desktop widths retain readable navigation, filters, rows, timestamps, original order amounts, detail links and page recovery actions. No blocking layout defect was observed.
Long generated order numbers wrap in the A06 table. They are visible in full; the layout does not hide their tails or turn them into an ellipsis.

The paid-order A07 confirmation shows order number and asks the operator to verify shipping before the distinct confirmation button; its teaching text says no real logistics and no repeated inventory deduction.
After the actual browser shipment action, admin and user screenshots show the corresponding same order, original snapshot and payment receipt with SHIPPED status and matching displayed shipment time.
Completed seed-state A07 is read-only. The future STEP12 customer-details location is plain text, without an active customer-details link.
Shipping values in A07/U08 are concealed by three opaque grey masks. Other captured pages have no shipping panel.
The focused existing skip link appears in the two paid-confirmation full-page captures; its visibility is explicitly recorded, not mistaken for hidden/removed content.
limitations: AI review of these exact PNGs does not replace named group-member acceptance, assistive-technology testing or mobile verification.

Screenshots do not independently prove 303 status, CSRF validation, exact query-string preservation, transaction isolation, first lock order, affected row count, seven-table zero-write branches, timestamps at microsecond precision or invariance after replay. Use the archived raw HTTP/DOM/native/database records for those claims.

The browser actually submitted the shipment and missing-CSRF requests; the screenshot is the resulting page, not the redirect trace. Before/after seven-table records and the 303 response/GET follow-up are separate evidence.

Recipient, phone and full address are intentionally masked and therefore cannot be visually validated from these images. No session identifier, CSRF original or plaintext password appears in this review report.
Full-page PNG heights exceed 768/1080 where the page scrolls. This does not claim all panels appeared above the fold.

The two viewport runs are sequential; each uses its own new 85.00 shipment fixture. Corresponding admin/user pairs within one viewport refer to the same order, while generated order numbers can differ between viewports.
No concurrency or fault injection is claimed; those remain STEP13.

native_log_crosscheck.null_actor_note: Null actor is separately rejected with zero SQL; there is no fabricated SQL/isolation observation for that branch.
native_log_crosscheck.scope: Actual private-DB AdminOrderService sequential shipping and state/identity checks; no fixture writes, HTTP, concurrency or fault injection
native_log_crosscheck.note: Read from actual saved log; this visual review did not rerun Service/database actions.
